[sewer-stormwater-gapfill] 123 entries (47 detailed, 76 roster) across 30 states (AR, CA, CO, CT, IA, ID, IL, IN, KY, MA, MD, ME, MN, MO, MS, NC, NH, NJ, NY, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TX, UT, VA, WA, WI, WV). Roster source: EPA Clean Watersheds Needs Survey 2022 (HydroShare mirror of the official CWNS CSVs; FACILITIES, POPULATION_WASTEWATER, POINT_OF_CONTACT, PHYSICAL_LOCATION, FACILITY_PERMIT tables). All 1,577 end-of-line POTWs with total residential population served >25,000 (1,238 responsible entities) were extracted to rosters/sewer_potw_cwns2022_over25k.csv. Entities were kept only if their name indicates a sewer-specific authority/district (sewerage/sanitary/sanitation/WPCA/water reclamation/utilities authority, etc.); city- and county-run combined water+sewer utilities were treated as already covered by the water-*.json files (their sewer charge is on the same bill). Every candidate was checked against all categories/*.json (water, sewer and name-token matching plus a manual alias list) and excluded if present - e.g., ALCOSAN, NEORSD, MSD Louisville/Cincinnati/St. Louis, WSSC, DC Water, MWRD Chicago, MMSD, NKY SD1, HRSD, DELCORA, LASA, SacSewer, Central San, LACSD, OCSD, Clean Water Services, WES, Johnson County Wastewater, Greater Peoria, UCSD, Duckett Creek, Fox Metro, Jefferson County AL, New Castle County DE, Sussex County DE. 16 billers researched in an earlier pass of this task were removed because they are already detailed in the sibling file sewer-stormwater-separate-billers.json (NHSA, GTMUA, Upper St. Clair, Suffolk County, AlexRenew, Muncie, Terre Haute, Richmond IN, Kokomo, Trumbull County, Oro Loma, NapaSan, Leucadia, Clark Regional, Snyderville Basin, Brunswick ME); that file should be read together with this one. Roster entries flag agencies that are likely wholesale/regional treatment only (households pay via town or water bill); these are included so a senior who sees the agency's name on a bill can identify it. Detailed entries record HOW the charge is billed (own bill, on the water/municipal bill, or on the property-tax roll), payment processor, pay-by-phone and assistance where published. Stormwater: standalone fees covered include WVSA (PA), Mt. Lebanon (PA), Montgomery County MD WQPC (tax bill), Fairfield-Suisun drainage charge (tax roll), Denver storm drainage. Limits: the web-search budget was exhausted early in this pass, so detailed research was limited to billers whose official domain could be reached directly; several sites were blocked by bot challenges (North Shore WRD IL, Huntington WV WQB) and were not bypassed. REVIEWER PASS 2026-09-30 (skeptical second pass): (1) Accuracy: the reviewer re-fetched the official pages for 30 of 36 original detailed entries and checked every stored URL for HTTP status. All stored URLs resolve except WVSA, Rockland County, Medina County and FRWRD, which return 403 or bot challenges to automated requests; they were kept from the earlier pass and noted as not re-fetched. Denver's storm-drainage URLs had moved and were updated to their redirect targets. Material corrections: Hammond Sanitary District charges are billed on the Hammond Water Works bill (pay link, pay-by-phone and processor added). MSD of Buncombe County's billing policy says most customers are billed by their water provider, and only well-water homes and industries get a bill from MSD. Upper Allen Township now uses Invoice Cloud and has a pay-by-phone line; autopay, paperless and history links were filled. Towamencin's sale of its sewer system to PA American Water was terminated, so the township still bills. WMUA's senior/disabled rate is confirmed ($79/qtr vs $128). Missing link fields (autopay_cancel, statements_history, paperless, login) and processors were also filled where official pages show them: Sanford = Municipal Online Payments, Thorn Creek = Illinois E-Pay/Collector Solutions, UAJA = Municipay/NPS, South Davis = BillingDoc, Kitsap = Point & Pay paperless. (2) Completeness: all 1,238 CWNS >25k responsible entities were re-screened against every categories/*.json file. The reviewer added new detailed entries for LEXserv (Lexington KY sewer, stormwater and landfill bill, separate from Kentucky American Water, with an income-based sewer/landfill fee program), the Lower Paxton Township Authority (PA sewer plus stormwater) and West County Wastewater (CA, collected on the property-tax roll). UMHJSA (PA) was upgraded from roster to detailed, and a roster entry was added for the Sangamon County WRD (IL, 150k+ people served; billing method not published). Official websites were found and confirmed by fetch for 33 roster agencies. Three duplicates were removed because they are already covered in water files: MLTMUA (water-northeast), Acme ID/Village of Wellington (water-south) and City of Lincoln NE LTU (water-central). Checked and not added: York City PA sewer (acquired by Pennsylvania American Water on 5/27/2022, so it is billed on the PAWC bill); Hamilton Twp NJ, Stark and Mahoning OH, Saratoga County SD1 and GNHWPCA, Bridgeport, Stamford and Norwalk WPCAs (already in sewer-stormwater-separate-billers.json or water-northeast.json); Nassau and Westchester County sewer districts (funded through county property-tax levies, with no separate charge or bill to research). Most remaining NJ/MA/WI/VA/WA roster agencies are wholesale treatment authorities, so households pay them through a town or water bill. Limits: the WebSearch budget was exhausted before this review started, so new billers could only be researched when an official domain could be found from a city site link, a sitemap or a probe of the likely domain. Websites for Middletown Township SA (NJ), Long Branch SA, Lake Stevens Sewer District, South Valley Sewer District (UT), North Shore WRD, Huntington WQB and Bloomington-Normal WRD could not be confirmed, so those stay roster entries with website null (Gary SD's linked domain did not respond). REVIEW CONTINUATION 2026-09-30 (after web search became available again): upgraded seven roster agencies that bill households directly to detailed after fetching their official pages: North Shore WRD (IL; its own bimonthly treatment bill, paid via Illinois ePAY, with a summer credit), Huntington WV Water Quality Board (formerly the Sanitary Board; pays through NexBillPay), Long Branch SA and TOMSA (NJ; quarterly bills on Edmunds WIPP), Lake Stevens Sewer District (WA; Xpress Bill Pay, with a 25% low-income senior/disabled Reduced Rate Program), Gary Sanitary District (IN; domain is now garysanitary.gov) and Bernards Township SA (NJ; semiannual bill from the township Tax Collector). The Landis SA website was confirmed. FRWRD now points its pay, autopay and paperless links to the City of Elgin bill, which collects the FRWRD 'Sewer Treatment' charge. The Montgomery County MD WQPC entry gained the property-tax pay portal, pay-by-phone, the lockbox address and the hardship-exemption eligibility (170% FPL or MEAP). Gap re-check: Spartanburg Sanitary Sewer District is billed on the Spartanburg Water bill (water-south.json). Delaware County OH RSD, ReWa, Stark County and Hamilton Twp NJ are already in sewer-stormwater-separate-billers.json. Butler, Warren and Clermont County OH water & sewer are in water-central.json. Scranton sewer was sold to PA American Water.

[sewer-stormwater-separate-billers] in progress

[territories-utilities-gov] Checked against the territory rows of rosters/electric_utilities.csv (EIA-861: PREPA 1,511,847 customers; Guam Power Authority 53,559; VI WAPA 54,457; CNMI CUC 17,555; ASPA 12,684 - all five have detailed entries) and rosters/water_systems_large.csv (EPA SDWIS: every large PR system belongs to PRASA/AAA, Guam systems to GWA; CUC and ASPA provide water in CNMI/AS; WAPA provides potable water in the USVI), so every territory resident's electric and water biller is covered. Electric in PR: LUMA Energy bills all PREPA/AEE customers; Genera PR (New Fortress) only operates PREPA's legacy power plants and does not bill customers, so it has no entry. Behind-the-meter solar lessors in PR/GU/VI on EIA (Sunnova ~54k PR customers, Sunrun ~28k PR) bill separately for solar leases/PPAs but are out of scope here. Government: PR property tax (CRIM), PR income tax (Hacienda/SURI), PR marbete/driver services (CESCO/DTOP), Guam DRT income tax and real property tax (PayGuam), Guam vehicle registration renewal (MyGuamTax; the reviewer corrected an earlier pointer to myid.guam.gov, which is the driver's-license/ID portal), USVI BIR income tax, USVI Tax Collector property tax, USVI BMV, CNMI Division of Revenue and Taxation, American Samoa Tax Office. Propane: Tropigas and Empire Gas (PR) are detailed here and also appear as roster entries in propane-heating-oil.json. Not duplicated here because they exist elsewhere: AutoExpreso (PR tolls, dmv-tolls-municipal.json), Liberty Puerto Rico and Claro Puerto Rico (cable/internet/landline/wireless files), Triple-S and MCS (medicare-health-insurance.json); also already elsewhere: Viya and GTA/Teleguam, IT&E (CNMI), Bluesky (AS), Banco Popular/FirstBank PR, PR public housing and ASUME. Trash: Puerto Rico municipalities generally fund residential trash collection from municipal revenue (CRIM/IVU) and do not send separate household trash bills; USVI and CNMI likewise have no household trash bill found; ASPA bills solid waste on its combined utility bill; Guam Solid Waste Authority does bill about 20,000 curbside households monthly; the reviewer found its official site (gswa.guam.gov) and upgraded it to detailed. Limits this session: web search quota was exhausted partway through, so later research relied on direct fetches of official sites; several official pages render with JavaScript or refused automated fetch (GPA financial-assistance page 403, ADSEF site refused connection, guamtax.com contact page blank). Reviewer pass 2026-09-30: every URL in the file was status-checked with curl (all resolve; lumapr.com returns 403 and guamwaterworks.org returns 429 to curl, so those pages were re-read with a fetch tool). Page content was re-read for 25+ entries' links. Changes: GSWA upgraded from roster to detailed. Guam MVD entry corrected to the MyGuamTax renewal and verified. Guam DRT income-tax and RPT entries got phones, mailing address, the MyGuamTax 'How to pay your 1040' page and the Senior Citizen & Disability real property tax credit. CESCO URLs updated for the web.cescodigital.pr.gov redirect, and the marbete pay_bill now points to Hacienda's colecturía directory, which lists marbete renewal. AAA got its separate payment and correspondence PO boxes, CUC got a payment-arrangements link, and ASPA notes now cover the CashPower prepaid option. CNMI and American Samoa levy essentially no residential real property tax bill, so no property-tax entries exist for them. Web search was unavailable to the reviewer (quota exhausted), so new billers could be found only by probing official domains.

Added all remaining active community water systems serving 3,300-50,000 people in the 13 states from EPA Envirofacts SDWIS WATER_SYSTEM (about 2,030 systems; institutional/military/university systems excluded) as roster tier with SDWIS regulatory-contact phone; ~60 of these are districts of Illinois/Indiana/Missouri/Iowa American Water, Aqua Ohio/Illinois and Citizens Water and inherit the parent's detailed billing links. Private companies covered: American Water (IL, IN, IA, MO), Essential Utilities/Aqua (OH, IL, IN), Citizens Energy (IN), Central States Water Resources/Confluence Rivers (MO), Superior Water Light & Power (WI), Del-Co (OH); Liberty Utilities (Missouri) water & sewer now has a detailed entry (Kubra EZ-PAY; its SDWIS districts point to it). Nexus Water Group (ex-Utilities Inc/Corix) lists no service areas in these states. Directly-billing sewer districts added: NEORSD, MSD St. Louis, MSD Cincinnati (via GCWW), Oakland County WRC, Johnson County Wastewater, Greater Peoria SD, Four Rivers (Rockford), Urbana-Champaign SD, Fox Metro, Downers Grove SD, West Branch (former Wheaton SD), Duckett Creek SD, Northwestern Water & Sewer District; property-tax-funded MWRD/MMSD/GLWA included as routing entries. Fixes: the Dearborn Heights LIHWAP link (404) was removed and its new BS&A auto-pay added. Lakewood OH's dead ezsecurepay portal (expired certificate) was replaced with the PayRazr portal from the city page. For St. Charles County PWSD 2, pwsd2.com turned out to be Jefferson County PWSD 2 (High Ridge) and pwsd2.org is Jackson County PWSD 2, so the entry was downgraded to roster with its SDWIS phone. (2) Re-fetched and corrected or filled 18 existing detailed entries: Kenosha, Farmington Hills/Pontiac/OCWRC (new mywrcaccount portal, autopay form, hardship program), MSD Cincinnati (CAP 25% senior discount), Del-Co, St. Louis Water (tornado affordability program), Norman (new MyUtility portal), Canton, Genesee County, Palatine, Flint, Warren County OH, Hammond and Evanston. Clermont County was mislabeled investor-owned and is now county. (3) Upgraded the 20 largest roster systems to detailed after fetching their pages: Aqua Illinois-Kankakee (a >50k system that had been left bare), Saginaw, Delta Twp, Warren OH, Redford, West Bloomfield, Enid, Newark OH, Elkhart, O'Fallon IL, Sheboygan, Chesterfield Twp, Monroe MI, Roseville MI, Battle Creek, Holland BPW, Huber Heights, Muskogee, Wentzville, Bartlesville and Moline. (4) Added Liberty Utilities (Missouri) and linked 5 Northwestern Water & Sewer District service areas to the District. Merged duplicate roster rows into SWL&P and Avon Lake Regional Water. Built by ov25.py. KNOWN GAPS: of the sites that were bot-blocked in the second pass, Grand Island NE, West Allis WI, Wauwatosa WI, Delaware OH, Salina KS, Marion IA, Olathe KS (pay page), Quincy IL and Downers Grove IL were re-read in the 2026-09-30 backfill (several through a real browser). Still blocked or unconfirmed: Eagan MN (SiteGround CAPTCHA - roster only), Cape Girardeau MO (CAPTCHA - website recorded unverified), Mason City IA (403 to every fetcher - detailed but verified=false), West Des Moines IA (unverified), Kenosha WI (city pages blocked; portal verified), Youngstown OH and Bloomington IL keep earlier data; systems under 3,300 population (roughly 10,000 small towns, rural water districts, mobile-home parks) are not listed - use SDWIS by ZIP/city for those; roster-tier entries lack websites and billing links; other directly-billing sanitary districts (e.g., Bloomington-Normal WRD, Sanitary District of Decatur, Gary/Hammond sanitary districts, Carmel Clay Regional Waste District, Fox River WRD, Thorn Creek Basin SD, Summit County DSSS) were not reached and are not yet entries; municipal stormwater fees usually appear on the city water bill. St. Charles County PWSD 2 (O'Fallon MO, about 100k people) was resolved in the 2026-09-30 backfill (waterdistrict2.com, AuthorityPay) and is now detailed. Many SDWIS owner-type codes are 'private' for systems that are really cities or co-ops, so entity_type on roster rows is approximate. Raytown Water Company (MO, private) is still roster only because its site did not resolve. ROSTER BACKFILL (2026-09-30): (1) Websites: at the start of the backfill 1995 roster rows had no website. Official sites were found by script - the domain of each system's EPA SDWIS contact email and city/village domain patterns (e.g. cityof<name>.com, <name><st>.gov, ci.<name>.<st>.us) - and accepted only when the homepage was fetched and its title matched the system/city (pages that answer curl with Cloudflare/Akamai/SiteGround challenges were loaded in a real browser and their titles checked; parked or unrelated domains such as westplains.com (farm dealer), ISP/telecom, engineering-firm and contract-operator email domains were rejected). A pay_bill link was added when the homepage exposed one (processor recorded from the link: Municipal Online Services/Tyler, Invoice Cloud, BS&A, Paymentus, PSN, Community Connect, AuthorityPay, SmartHub, etc.). About 30 domains that only return a SiteGround/Cloudflare CAPTCHA are recorded from the SDWIS email domain with verified=false. Now 1512 roster rows have a website and 1078 have a pay_bill link; 418 rows still have no website - mostly small rural water districts, PWSDs and mobile-home/tribal systems whose SDWIS contact uses a free e-mail address (gmail/yahoo/ISP) and which often have no public site; for those the SDWIS regulatory phone remains the contact. (2) Thin states: upgraded the largest 10k-50k city utilities to detailed with view/pay/autopay/cancel/history links, phones and processor - KS (Salina, Hutchinson, Leavenworth Waterworks, Garden City, Dodge City, Derby, Emporia, Gardner, Hays, Pittsburg, Liberal, Junction City, Newton, Great Bend, McPherson BPU, Haysville, Winfield), IA (Urbandale, Marion, Cedar Falls Utilities, Mason City, Waukee, Marshalltown Water Works, Ottumwa Water Works, Muscatine Power & Water, Johnston, North Liberty, Clive, Grimes, Warren Water District, Coralville), WI (Neenah, De Pere, Fitchburg, Menomonee Falls, Franklin, Marshfield Utilities, South Milwaukee, Cudahy, Ashwaubenon, Howard, West Allis, Wauwatosa, Manitowoc Public Utilities, Watertown, Bellevue), NE (Grand Island, Beatrice BPW, Scottsbluff plus the earlier Papillion, Kearney, Fremont, Norfolk, North Platte, Hastings, Columbus), ND (Dickinson plus earlier backfill), SD (earlier backfill). Detailed water entries by state now: IA 26, IL 63, IN 37, KS 25, MI 39, MN 19, MO 25, ND 9, NE 12, OH 49, OK 12, SD 10, WI 28. (3) Retried blocked sites as listed under KNOWN GAPS. Web search quota ran out partway, so later work used site crawling and a real browser only. Senior/low-income help captured where the utility publishes it (e.g. Newton KS $100 senior credit, Hutchinson KS senior low-income program, West Allis LIWAP referrals, MP&W Project Share, Coralville Neighbors Helping Neighbors, Kearney/Fremont third-party notification). [water-northeast] REVIEWER PASS 2026-09-30 (skeptical second pass on link-backfill-water-northeast; file edited in place, no new file). Fill rates across the 502 detailed entries after review: view_bill 43%, pay_bill 100%, autopay_setup 44%, autopay_cancel 44%, statements_history 32%, paperless 36%, payment_assistance 39%, pay-by-phone 34%, payment_processor 91% (was ~90%); 484 of 502 detailed entries verified (was 469). What the reviewer did: (a) HTTP status sweep of all 1,648 unique URLs on detailed entries (1,504 returned 200; 106 returned 403 and 23 returned 202 from bot protection, not dead links; 11 failed to connect; 1 returned 500). The failures were re-read in a real browser: Pennichuck and Kittery pages are fine (script-blocked only); Brattleboro's Official Payments utility link returns HTTP 500 and was replaced by the Town's OpenGov portal and pay page; otda.ny.gov/programs/ no longer lists a water program. (b) Hand-read about 30 entries' pages in a browser, prioritizing the unverified ones: Baltimore, OCWA, Providence Water, York Water, PVWC, Chester WA, Springfield WSC, Wilmington DE, Lehigh County Authority, Manchester Water Works, Charles County, Newton, Town of Hempstead, Jamestown BPU, Brattleboro, St Albans, Verona, Farmington ME, Brunswick-Topsham, COMM, Colonie/Latham, New Bedford (Invoice Cloud), Weir River, Trenton, Clinton NJ, Riverhead. 16 were changed to verified=true. (c) Fixes: St Albans VT pay and autopay links pointed to a calendar item ('Water bills due') and now point to the Online Payments & Autopay page, with the City Hall phone-payment line added; Newton's autopay URL now redirects, so it points to the Make a Payment page; Manchester NH statements_history and view_bill now point to the official Customer Account Information page (which says bill copies and payment/bill history are available online), and its pay-by-phone number (603) 624-6494 option 2 is confirmed; Verona URLs were changed to the canonical tax_utility page; Waynesboro's statements_history pointed to the homepage and is now null; Hempstead's payment_assistance pointed to the generic OTDA programs page and now points to the Water Department page, noting that NYS LIHWAP may no longer be taking applications; Jamestown BPU pay-by-phone (716) 661-1660 ext. 3 was added. Payment processors were filled for 5 entries from vendor links on their official pay pages (MerchantTransact, Government Window, 3 Edmunds WIPP). (d) Completeness: the >50k systems named in the brief are all at detailed tier (COMM, Latham/Colonie, New Bedford, Kiryas Joel, and Hyannis). Kiryas Joel (Cloudflare 'you have been blocked') and the New Bedford city site (Cloudflare verification loop) still cannot be read, even in a real browser, so their city-page links stay null. West View Water Authority now shows a SiteGround robot challenge and was not re-verified. No CAPTCHA or challenge was solved. No duplicates were found (name plus state). No new billers were added: the roster was already reconciled against EPA SDWIS by earlier passes, and web search was unavailable to this reviewer (session quota used up). Remaining known gaps: 18 detailed entries remain unverified (bot-blocked sites, including West View, Old Bridge MUA, Wayne Twp, Meriden, Franklin Twp NJ, ACMUA, Kiryas Joel, and small vendor-portal-only systems). About 280 small-system detailed rows were filled by script and only status-checked plus keyword-checked; the random sample of 10 had 2 bad links (St Albans, Waynesboro), both now fixed, so similar errors likely remain in about 1 in 5 of those rows. The Edmunds WIPP public pages do not document autopay, paperless or history. Separate sewer billers are only partly covered, and systems serving fewer than 3,000 people are not listed. --- PRIOR PASS NOTES --- LINK BACKFILL 2026-09-30 (category link-backfill-water-northeast). Fill rates across the 502 detailed entries (the task brief's starting figures, then the figures at the start of this pass, then now): view_bill 17% then 30% now 43%; autopay_setup 25% then 33% now 44%; autopay_cancel 19% then 31% now 44%; statements_history 17% then 22% now 32%; paperless 29% then 36%; payment_assistance 11% then 23% now 39%; pay-by-phone 32% then 34%; payment_processor about 90%. Method: (1) Reused a crawl of about 12,600 official and vendor pages (3 link levels from each entry's website, pay, help and login URLs). Added about 1,150 pages found through site sitemaps (sitemap.xml and wp-sitemap for 257 of 398 hosts), then regex-scanned every page for autopay, paperless, bill-history, bill-explainer and assistance wording near water, sewer or bill context. Every candidate snippet (about 600) was read by hand before it was accepted. Rejected: property-tax-only pages, news and agenda pages, generic vendor legal terms, and 'we do not offer autopay' pages (Brick MUA and Kittery say so in their notes). (2) Vendor portals: for 44 Invoice Cloud entries, the biller's own Invoice Cloud Sign In page (customerlogin.aspx?billerguid=..., stored without the session token) lists Review Invoice History, Review Payment History and Schedule Automatic Payments. It is used for statements_history and autopay_setup/cancel, the 'Pay or View Bills' portal page is used for view_bill, and IVR pay-by-phone numbers were taken from the portal pages. AuthorityPay (Muni-Link) register pages (e-bill/AutoPay), ePayUB portal pages (Auto Pay, Billing History, Bill Preference), Xpress Bill Pay org pages (automatic payments) and Municipal Online Payments pages were scanned the same way. Edmunds GovTech WIPP portals (about 95 NJ/PA entries) were rendered in a browser. They only say that registered users can 'schedule payments' (no autopay, e-bill or history text on the public page), so they were not used for those fields. (3) Sites that block scripts (OCWA, MAWC, Chester WA, Worcester, Harford, Wilmington DE, Providence Water, Barnstable) were read in a real browser. Only automatic browser checks were waited out; no CAPTCHAs were solved. (4) State programs: the NJ DCA Winter Termination Program (fetched) was added to senior_programs for all 73 NJ municipal/authority detailed entries. Its page is used as payment_assistance for the 40 of them that have no utility-specific assistance page (they carry a note saying so). The federal/state LIHWAP programs have ended: the NJ DCA LIHWAP page now returns 404, and the NY OTDA and PA DHS LIHWAP pages are gone or unreachable. Local pages that still mention LIHWAP were not used as live assistance links. NYC's HWAP (fetched) is on the NYC DEP entry. No statewide MA water-discount program exists; local elderly discounts were captured where found (for example Lowell elderly water-rate discount, Worcester Clause 41C, Ramsey NJ senior discount, Portsmouth NH water/sewer assistance). (5) Roster upgrades: COMM (Barnstable), Town of Colonie/Latham WD, New Bedford and Kiryas Joel were already detailed at the start of this pass. The Hyannis Water System (Town of Barnstable, 7,577 connections) was upgraded to detailed from the Water Supply Division page and its ePayUB portal. Remaining gaps: many small municipal systems simply do not document autopay, paperless or history on public pages. Those features are either absent or exist only after login, and entries say so in notes where checked. Kiryas Joel (Cloudflare hard block), newbedford-ma.gov and the Latham Invoice Cloud vanity page (JavaScript-only) could not be read. PA and NY municipal systems have few assistance programs beyond payment plans. Pages were read on 2026-09-30, but about 280 smaller rows still rest on script-extracted evidence rather than a full human read. PREVIOUS NOTES: 1353 entries (496 detailed, 857 roster; 501 verified). REVIEW PASS 2026-09-29 (second-pass reviewer): (a) Checked every URL in every detailed entry with an HTTP fetch (1,332 unique URLs): 1,216 returned 200, 81 returned 403 and 22 returned 202 bot-challenges (site blocks automation, not necessarily broken), 3 returned 404 and were removed or replaced (Frederick MD Citizen Access Portal, Hampden Twp utility-assist page, a City Hall Systems help video), and a Proofpoint-wrapped link (Carle Place WD) was replaced with the direct Forte URL. (b) Hand-reviewed about 45 of the largest detailed entries against their fetched pay/FAQ pages. Filled autopay_cancel, statements_history, paperless, payment_assistance and pay-by-phone numbers where the page supported it (American Water PA/NJ, Aqua, Aquarion, ECWA, DC Water, Connecticut Water, RWA, Anne Arundel, Trenton Water Works (rebuilt: Invoice Cloud portal, 24-hr pay line, city-vs-township sewer billing), Rochester, Buffalo, BWSC, Artesian, Erie Water Works, Middlesex, Tidewater, Portland Water District, PVWC, Springfield, Harford, WPJWA, North Penn, Easton Suburban, LCA, Manchester Water Works, Yonkers, Kent County WA, Pawtucket, Capital Region Water). Where autopay is managed only inside the online account, autopay_cancel points to the page that describes autopay and the notes say so. HI has only four public water billers (Honolulu BWS, Maui DWS, Hawaii County DWS, Kauai DOW) plus Hawaii Water Service - all detailed; 16 HI county sub-system roster rows now point to their county department's site; military/hospital systems are not residential billers. Added verified official websites to 13 roster rows (guessed domains accepted only when the fetched home page named the city/district and state). Removed 10 help_center_url values that pointed to unrelated city FAQs. Inferred payment_processor for 21 entries from payment links on official pages. Detailed-entry fill rates now: view_bill 62%, autopay_cancel 30%, statements_history 53%, payment_assistance 62%, autopay_setup 76%, paperless 57%. STILL MISSING: ~50 large detailed billers' sites return HTTP 403 to automated fetches (e.g., Long Beach, North Las Vegas, Gilbert, TVWD, AWWU, Salem OR, Tempe, Pomona, Waco, Fullerton, Carrollton, Santa Clara, Skagit PUD, Yuma, Las Cruces, Palo Alto, Bend, Kirkland, Tigard, Goodyear, Prescott, Carson City, Homer) so their remaining links could not be verified; many utilities publish no autopay-cancellation instructions at all (cancel is done inside the Paymentus/Invoice Cloud/Municipal Online Payments portal, which is login-only), so autopay_cancel stays null rather than guessed. About 1,230 roster rows still lack websites (mostly Texas MUDs and small WA systems); a web-search budget cap stopped further website confirmation this pass. REVIEWER PASS 2026-09-30 (second, skeptical): (1) Completeness: re-checked against rosters/water_systems_large.csv - all 423 western PWSIDs in that roster are present (0 missing). Upgraded 10 more large roster systems to detailed from official pages fetched this session: Elk Grove WD, Diablo WD, Indian Wells Valley WD, South Coast WD (CA); Green Mountain WSD, City of Northglenn (CO); Riverton City, Spanish Fork City (UT); City of Camarillo (CA); City of Duncanville (TX). (2) Accuracy: HTTP-checked all ~2,080 URLs on detailed entries (1,659 200, ~400 403 bot-blocks, 3 404s, a few timeouts) and hand-checked ~35 entries. Fixed: 3 truncated FormCenter URLs (Pasadena TX autopay_cancel, Bremerton paperless, Woodinville); San Jose Muni Water view_bill pointing to San Jose Clean Energy (electric) and help URL pointing to the Homelessness FAQ; Buena Park help -> homeless FAQ; login/help URLs pointing to surveys, start-service or alarm-permit forms (Sweetwater, Cedar Park, La Habra, South Jordan, Wichita Falls, Baytown, Alhambra, Valley County WD); junk pay-by-phone values 'phone' (Round Rock, Brighton, Padre Dam, Woodinville, Victorville); corrected Round Rock, Brighton, Padre Dam, Woodinville phones from fetched pages; Woodinville processor is doxo (WaterSmart is only the usage portal); removed Bakersfield's 408-367-8593 (a Cal Water SDWIS contact, not a city billing line); stripped tracking params from NBU login; Homer AK now verified. (3) Added: Garland CAP payment_assistance, SacSewer autopay_cancel (explicit 'stop EFT' wording), Garden Grove view/history/pay-by-phone, Plano view_bill; 7 verified websites for roster rows (Brea, Cerritos, Haltom City, Laguna Madre WD, Rockett SUD, King County WD 20, Travis County WCID 17). A second automated scan of every detailed entry's pay/autopay/help page for explicit cancel wording found only one new genuine instruction (SacSewer) - most western water utilities do not publish autopay-cancel steps outside their login portals. Detailed per thin state: MT 11, WY 11, NM 12, AK 10, ID 12, NV 13, HI 5 (all HI retail billers). About 1,215 roster rows (mostly small Texas MUD/WSC systems) still lack a website.

entries.notes: NSWRD sends its OWN bimonthly sewage-treatment bill, separate from the village/city water-and-sewer bill (the municipal bill covers only local sewer lines). ACH auto-pay: download the authorization form and email it to ach@northshorewrd.org; no cancellation steps are published, so call the district. No paperless or online history page was found. entries.service_area_detail: Lexington / Fayette County, KY. Separate monthly city bill for sanitary sewer, water quality (stormwater) management fee and landfill fee; water itself is billed by Kentucky American Water

entries.senior_programs: Sewer and Landfill User Fee Program (through Community & Resident Services, 859-300-5300) pays part of the monthly sewer, water quality and landfill fees for income-eligible residents who re-certify every year. The city also offers LEXserv financial aid if water is about to be shut off over a past-due LEXserv bill. Winter averaging (Average Winter Consumption) caps the sewer charge based on Nov-Apr water use.
entries.notes: LEXserv is Lexington's own utility bill, separate from the Kentucky American Water bill. It carries the sanitary sewer fee (based on water use, with winter averaging), the water quality (stormwater) management fee per ERU ($6.18/ERU from July 1, 2026) and a landfill fee. The Customer Portal is used to view the current bill and billing history, pay or schedule payments, sign up for ACH, AutoPay or paperless billing, and set up payment plans. ACH auto-pay has no fee and is set up and cancelled under Forms > 'LEXserv manage ACH automatic payment' (both steps are on the same page). Card AutoPay goes through Invoice Cloud. You can also pay by text, by phone, at the drop box at 200 E. Main St, at the Revenue Payment Center at 218 E. Main St (M-F 8-4:30), or by mail. An unpaid LEXserv bill can lead to Kentucky American shutting off your water. Also see trash-municipal-gapfill.json for the LFUCG landfill fee.

entries.name: Lower Paxton Township Authority (PA) - sewer & stormwater billing
entries.parent_company: Lower Paxton Township, Dauphin County, PA
entries.service_area_detail: Lower Paxton Township (Harrisburg suburbs, Dauphin County); water is from Pennsylvania American Water / other providers
entries.payment_processor: Logics online bill pay (newolbp.logicshosted.com) - 2.95% fee on card/e-check payments of $85 or more, $2.50 under $85
entries.notes: The township sends property owners a quarterly bill, in arrears, each January, April, July and October. It covers the residential sewer flat rate ($163 per quarter), the stormwater fee ($26 per quarter for single-family homes) and solid waste. Homes on septic still get the stormwater and solid-waste bill. The township does NOT take payments by phone. ACH auto-debit is free: mail the authorization form with a voided check at least a month before the billing month; drafts run on the 1st of Feb, May, Aug and Nov. The page does not say how to cancel, so call 717-657-5617. Unpaid bills get a 10% penalty and a $25 returned-payment fee, and delinquent accounts go to Portnoff Law Associates. Municipal Center: 425 Prince Street, Harrisburg, PA 17109. CWNS 2022 lists the Lower Paxton plant among POTWs serving >25k residents.
